status: Visual exploration; the existing website remains the baseline.
principle: Measure how quickly a reader forms a correct mental model.

prompts.name: 01-ledger-overview
prompts.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram.
Asset type: high fidelity visual exploration for Harmonia's architecture book, a single landscape editorial diagram, about 1600 by 1000, without browser chrome.
Input image 1 is the EXISTING COMPONENT MAP: use its actual architectural facts as the reference, but radically improve its information hierarchy. Input image 2 is the APPROVED WORKFLOW VISUAL STYLE: adopt its white canvas, pale blue grouping, navy typography, restrained electric-blue connections, softly dimensional miniature pictograms, rounded surfaces and generous space. Do not copy its financing story, people, carousel or buttons.

Reader: an impatient senior engineer seeing Harmonia for the first time. They should understand one thing at a glance: the common workflow model and participating applications live on the Canton ledger; the user-facing Dapp is above that boundary. They should feel oriented, not impressed by complexity. Make an exceptionally clear, beautiful, quiet diagram that is plausible to later implement with HTML and SVG. Large readable typography, expressive simple diagrams instead of card paragraphs.

Exact headline: "The workflow lives on the ledger."
Small brand: "Harmonia"
One dominant wide pale blue area labeled "Canton · Daml" with a small adjacent "ON LEDGER". Inside it, three spacious aligned responsibilities with soft sculpted white pictograms:
1. "Harmonia Core", subtitle "Workflow state + step rules", with a tiny clear three-node workflow motif.
2. "Binding DAR", subtitle "Application participation", with an elegant interface / socket pictogram.
3. "Application DARs", subtitle "Own templates + choices", with two separate application tiles and a modest lock detail.
Connect Core to Binding and Binding to applications by clean, quiet blue lines WITHOUT arrowheads; these are participation relationships, not transaction flow or package import direction. Leave generous space around connections.
Above that dominant ledger grouping, one visually quieter, much smaller off-ledger browser pictogram labeled "Harmonia Dapp", subtitle "Inspect · compose · submit". Its downward arrow crosses the ledger boundary near Core, labeled "Ledger API". The Dapp is an interaction surface, never a runtime workflow engine.
Below the main ledger group, one small secondary build-time strip, visibly subordinate, with exact labels "BUILD TIME", "App DAR", "Builder", "Binding DAR", connected in that order by fine dashed arrows. Tiny adjacent explanatory line: "Or implement the interfaces directly."
One calm sentence within the main ledger group near the application side: "Applications retain ownership, authorization and privacy."
Tiny neutral source credit at the foot: "Based on the original architecture · §1".

Do not reproduce the original's exhaustive field lists, legend, reference examples, repeated subtitles, arbitrary logos, prose paragraphs or open-design tables. Those belong in reference detail. Do not invent a package import direction, a central authority or a server executing the workflow. No buttons, links, menus, avatars or code dumps. The hierarchy should be unmistakable: headline, on-ledger relationship, supporting UI and build path. Never reduce readability to squeeze extra information in.

prompts.name: 02-step-execution
prompts.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram.
Asset type: high fidelity visual exploration for Harmonia's architecture book, a single landscape editorial diagram, about 1600 by 1000, without browser chrome.
Input image 1 is the ORIGINAL CONTRACT MODEL and is the factual reference. Input image 2 is the APPROVED WORKFLOW VISUAL STYLE: use its white canvas, pale blue grouping, navy typography, soft dimensional document pictograms, restrained blue connections and generous spacing. Do not copy its people, financing details, carousel or buttons.
This is a companion to an architecture overview, for an impatient senior engineer. Explain one thing: a workflow definition creates an instance, the instance assigns a step to an actor, and the assigned step reaches an application choice through an interface. Application authority remains intact. This is a focused reading of the original's main execution path, not a replacement of its full schema. Make the message extremely easy to take in, with one left-to-right path and only essential text.

Exact headline: "From a workflow to an application choice."
Small brand: "Harmonia"
One calm pale-blue ledger area labeled "Canton · Daml".
Within it show ONE uninterrupted, generously spaced left-to-right chain of FIVE elegant pictographic stations, with blue arrows correctly touching neither text nor pictograms:
1. A softly sculpted reusable plan/document icon. Label "Definition". Small exact original name below: "WorkflowDefinition".
2. A document with a small progress motif. Label "Instance". Small original name: "WorkflowInstance".
3. A small assignment document with actor/key motif. Label "Assigned step". Small original name: "StepAssignment".
4. A minimal interface/socket pictogram. Label "Step interface". Small original name: "HarmoniaStepAction".
5. An application tile containing a small diamond choice symbol. Label "App choice". Small original name: "AppTemplate".

Group the first three stations within a subtly lighter shared region labeled "Harmonia Core". Group only the final station inside a clearly bounded white area labeled "Application". The interface sits between these groups without implying a resolved package-import boundary.
Only two tiny relationship words above arrows, "creates" between 1 and 2 and "assigns" between 2 and 3. The remaining blue arrows show invocation through the interface toward the app choice.
Above the Assigned step station, one small key-shaped authority marker labeled "Assigned actor" with a fine connector into that station, visually subordinate to the main flow.
Below the Application tile, within its boundary, one succinct line: "Own authorization".
One short explanatory sentence below the main illustration: "The workflow coordinates. The application controls its choice."
Tiny neutral source note at the foot: "Original architecture · §2 · illustrative contract names".

No field lists, source-code samples, giant UML boxes, legends, prose paragraphs or arrows crossing other arrows. Do not add a return loop: continuation, branching and atomic blocks are separate explanations. Do not claim any original illustrative type name is implemented in the current code. No buttons, menus, links, avatars, extra labels or decorative cartoons. Preserve the serious, harmonious white-and-blue artistic direction of the approved reference while vastly improving the hierarchy and legibility of the original diagram.
